newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Friday due to overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange kerb market, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 19,080 yuan ($2,355) per tonne, down 60 yuan. It opened at 19,000 and hit a low of 18,950.
November ended unchanged at 18,900, December rose 100 to 19,030, January fell 70 to 19,070, March fell 80 to 19,070 and April fell 100 to 19,080.
Combined volume fell to 39,540 tonnes from 40,450.
Copper opened lower and short-covering pushed prices from lows for most of the session.
Traders said LME losses depressed long position holders but most contracts found support at the 19,000-yuan level.
"Most investors did not want to sell below the key support level of 19,000 and did not panic despite LME losses because they thought the short-term market trend was unclear," one trader said.
But traders said LME remained the major factor influencing Shanghai copper due to a lack of domestic market-moving news.
"Many investors are focussing on LME stockpile data tonight, which is likely to determine the short-term market direction," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mixed. November rose 100 to 13,500 yuan per tonne, December did not trade and January fell 90 to 13,210.
Combined volume rose to 610 tonnes from 220.
